module_title: Types of GST (CGST, SGST, IGST) and Tax Slabs
introduction: At this level, we will understand why your shopping bills show CGST, SGST, or IGST, and look at the different tax categories (Slabs) into which goods are divided in India.

core_concepts.title: Intra-State Sale (Within the State)
core_concepts.description:
When a good is sold within the same State (e.g., Delhi goods sold in Delhi), the GST is split into two equal halves: 
1. CGST (Central GST): This portion goes to the Central Government. 
2. SGST (State GST): This portion goes to that specific State Government.

core_concepts.title: Inter-State Sale (Between Two States)
core_concepts.description: When a good is sold from one State to another (e.g., Gujarat goods sold in Maharashtra), ONLY 'IGST' (Integrated GST) is applied. The Central Government collects the entire IGST and later shares half of it with the 'Destination State' (where the good was consumed—in this case, Maharashtra).

core_concepts.title: GST Tax Slabs
core_concepts.description:
There are 4 main tax slabs for goods and services in India: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%. 
(Essential items are kept at 0%, meaning tax-free). There are also special rates of 3% for Gold and 0.25% for rough diamonds.

core_concepts.title: Items Kept OUTSIDE GST
core_concepts.description:
This is highly tested! Some items still attract the old VAT and Excise duties and are NOT under GST: 
1. Alcohol for human consumption. 
2. 5 Petroleum Products (Crude oil, Petrol, Diesel, ATF/Aviation Fuel, and Natural Gas). 
3. Electricity.

important_entities.name: GSTN (Goods and Services Tax Network)
important_entities.significance: GSTN is a non-profit technology company that manages the massive IT system and the GST Portal, where all businesses register and file their tax returns.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often think IGST money is kept entirely by the Central Government. FALSE. IGST is 'collected' by the Center, but it is equally divided between the Center and the 'Destination State' (under Article 269A).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Examiners frequently ask, 'Which of the following is NOT a GST slab?' (They usually give 15% or 20% as the wrong option).

exam_strategy_tips: 'Alcohol for human consumption' is permanently kept out of GST by the Constitution itself, whereas Petroleum can be brought under GST in the future if the GST Council recommends it.
